steps: Placement & floor support

Set the unit on a level surface that carries it and its venting. Not directly on carpet, vinyl, tile or other combustibles other than wood flooring — use a metal or wood panel the full width and depth; build a solid, continuous platform if raised.

• Locate out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies — it produces a large amount of heat. Bedroom installation is allowed.
  • Where possible, position it so the vent terminates between two studs.
  • Floor protection in front isn't required; a combustible hearth extension may be used. The bottom of the fireplace must be level with the finished hearth for the safety barrier to fit (B41-PTF2: unit 2-1/4" above the finished hearth).
  • Outdoor covered installs (p. 16): operation approved 40°F to 110°F; roof overhang in front and to each side at least 1/2 of the roofline height above the fireplace base; black painted barriers recommended.
Stand-offs & nailing flanges

Form and attach the top stand-off brackets and heat shields before setting the unit — they give the 10" minimum to the header (non-combustible material only in that zone, full width). Fit the nailing flanges for the 1/4" side clearance; never remove them. Fit trim kit B41-FTK first if used.

1. Remove and save the (4) screws holding the stand-off heat shields and brackets on top.
  2. Bend each top stand-off bracket at the perforations; secure with the (4) saved screws plus the (4) on the fireplace top.
  3. Form the heat shields (flange up and to the back) and secure with (8) screws from the components packet.
  4. Nailing flanges: stand-off flanges face away from the unit; bend at the perforation until parallel with the face (not toward it); set the framing stud against the small stand-off.
No wood, sheetrock or other combustibles in the 10" header zone above the stand-offs.
Frame the rough opening
44-1/2" H × 41-3/8" W × 17-1/2" D with a single vertical header board. Allow for wall covering and facing thickness, and keep every Table 3.1 clearance (front 36", ceiling 31", sidewall 1").

• Metal-Fab vent: adapter 4DDA is required; it raises the vent centerline 3-3/4", and rear venting needs the enclosure 3-3/4" deeper.
  • Horizontal pass-throughs: 1" clearance top, bottom and sides of flex pipe; 1-1/2" top and 1" bottom and sides for rigid pipe. Use Kozy Heat #700-WPT (walls 4" to 6½") or a wall thimble with the 1" top clearance.
  • Vertical runs: 1" clearance on all sides. Insulate chase outside walls against cold air.
  • Leave room in front for barrier removal, gas line and service access.
  • Masonry facing: prepare a foundation for the full load and use a lintel over the unit.
Facing, mantel & safety barrier

Fit the supplied 42-7/8" × 10-1/2" non-combustible board (3/4" onto the framing sides, 1/2" onto the header). 3/4" trim from 5-1/2" and a 6" mantel from 9" above the top. Install the safety barrier — it is required.

• Combustible mantels may grow 1" deeper for each 1" higher, starting at the 6" mantel. With barrier B41-RSF2 only: trim from 1-1/2", 6" mantel from 5".
  • Non-combustible mantel: min 6" vertical clearance to a max 6" depth, then 1" up for every 1" deeper.
  • Adjacent sidewall 1" from the finishing edge (B41-PTF2: 3" from its outside edge).
  • Minimum non-combustible chamber height: 48" rear vent; 54" top vent, minimum horizontal, rigid pipe; 58" top vent, minimum horizontal, flex pipe.
  • Trim kit B41-FTK and the exterior trim kit (supplied with B41-RSF2) attach before the fireplace is installed.
  • Barrier gasket rope, where present, must touch the face or finish to achieve the mantel clearances.
  • To limit drywall cracking: dry, dust-free surfaces; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound such as Durabond; high-quality acrylic latex primer and finish; avoid flat or light-colored paints.
Gas line

Listed ½" tee-handle manual shut-off and flexible connector to the ½" valve inlet (a 3/8" × 18" connector and shut-off are supplied), run through the gas line hole and clear of the fan. Built for natural gas — convert to propane with the kit before fitting the light kit or logs.

• Gas line by a qualified person to local code, or ANSI Z223.1. Massachusetts: licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off during piping tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water.
  • Inlet supply: NG 5" – 10.5" WC (7" recommended); propane 12" – 13" WC.
  • Conversion kits (sold separately): propane LCK-B41L-SB, natural gas NCK-B41L-SB.
Termination location

Place the cap per the termination clearance table and never recess it into the wall or siding. Vertical caps follow the roof-pitch height table (1.0 ft for flat to 6/12). Don't connect to a chimney serving any other appliance.

Above grade, deck, porch12"
Openable window or door12" Canada · 9" US
Ventilated soffit (within 2 feet)24"
Unventilated soffit12"
Outside / inside corner0" / 12"
Mechanical air supply inlet6' Canada · 3' above if within 10' US
Between two terminations12"

A vent shall not terminate directly above a sidewalk or paved driveway that is located between two single family dwellings and serves both dwellings (footnote to the paved sidewalk or driveway row of the manual's termination table).

These clearances are to heat-resistant material, not vinyl; terminating against vinyl siding needs the vinyl siding protector supplied with the #700-2 kits. Massachusetts sidewall terminations less than 7 feet above finished grade carry carbon monoxide detector and signage requirements (p. 7).
Vent & restrictor

Approved 4" × 6-5/8" co-axial pipe within the run limits, ¼" rise per 12" on horizontal runs, max (4) 90° elbows. If restricting, slide the restrictor plate into the top exhaust, tabs toward you, before attaching the vent. Rear venting: move the collars and cover plates first.

• Rear vent: the unused exit must keep its cover plates. Move the 4" exhaust and 6-5/8" intake collars to the rear and the cover plates to the top before going further.
Maker's website: Venting, Rear-Vent Ready (top-vent convertible). Install to the manual.
  • Elbows: subtract 3' for each 90° after the first and 1½' for each 45°; (2) 45° elbows may replace (1) 90°.
  • #700-2 flex kits: top vent only; minimum bend radius 6" to center; don't stretch an extension beyond 6'.
  • #700-WPT wall pass-through: sections overlap at least 1-1/2"; walls thicker than 6-1/2" need an extension.
  • Restrictor: shipped with all inner rings in (most restriction); knock out the innermost ring for less, all inner rings for the least. It can also be fitted later through the fireplace baffle (see Pressure test & flame set-up).
  • Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.
Light kit, media & log set

Convert to propane first if needed. Fit the halogen bulbs with a soft cloth (never bare hands), crushed glass media in front of the burner with lava rock on top, then the ember panel and the 8-piece log set on the burner pins — never over the burner ports.

Disconnect all electric power before working on the light kit. Remove the safety barrier and glass valance, the log set and refractory panels (if installed), then the air deflector, burner assembly and burner heat shield to reach the (4) bulb receptacles; reinstall in reverse.

Traditional log set #B41-500

Ember panel in front of the burner; base logs BP1 to BP4 onto the burner pins; BP5 and BP6 into the base-log notches; BP7 and BP8 as shown in Figure 8.3.

Birchwood log set #B41-B501 (p. 41)

Ember panel in front; base logs 41B-1 to 41B-4 onto the pins; 41B-5 and 41B-6 into the notches; 41B-7 and 41B-8 as shown in Figure 8.4.

Log numbers are on the bottom of each log. Spread rockwool embers onto the logs and burner with a stiff bristle brush. Final log positions are shown only in the figures.

Logs over burner ports affect flame appearance and cause excessive soot on the logs and glass.
Power up & initialize

Grounded 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps supply, hot at all times with no switch. Rocker OFF, 4 AA in the backup holder, 3 AAA in the remote, connect AC. With the firebox cleared, press SW1 (3 beeps, amber LED) and the remote ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps, pilot lights).

1. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF.
  2. Install (4) AA batteries (not included) in the backup holder on the control module and (3) AAA (components packet) in the remote.
  3. Connect the IFC module to AC power.
  4. Remove all packaging and combustibles from the firebox — the next steps spark the igniter and light the pilot if gas is supplied.
  5. Press the red SW1 button: (3) beeps and an amber LED mean it's ready to pair.
  6. Within (5) seconds press the remote ON/OFF: (4) beeps confirm the code and the pilot lights.
  7. Press ON/OFF again; the pilot goes out, confirming the command.
  8. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation.

Manual operation without the remote (10.3): rocker OFF, press SW1 until (3) beeps and the amber LED, then press SW1 again within (5) seconds; the pilot lights and the rocker switch runs the burner on HI only. The control module housing is reached by lifting out the bottom frame, which must go back to maintain clearances.
Pressure test & flame set-up

Check inlet (IN tap) and manifold (OUT tap) pressures against the tables with a ¼" I.D. hose, then confirm each tap reseals. Burn 15 minutes, then fine-tune the venturi (factory NG 1/8", LP 5/8") and restrictor for lazy, yellow flames.

Dark orange, black tipsventuri closed too far → open slightly
Short, blue flamesventuri open too far → close slightly
Lifting (ghosting)gas pressure too high or venturi closed too far → check manometer, open venturi slightly
Short, flickeringexcessive draft → add restrictor
Lifting or ghosting (draft)insufficient draft → remove inner ring(s) or the restrictor
Note: for a flame that burns blue and lifts off the burner, the troubleshooting chart on p. 54 says to open the air shutter slightly; Table 11.4 on p. 51 says short, blue flames mean the venturi is open too far (close slightly), and p. 51 adds that opening the shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift.

Venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician: remove the barrier, glass, logs and burner; loosen the venturi screw, adjust in slight increments, retighten. Check log placement before adjusting for soot. The restrictor is reached through the termination access panel on the baffle ((2) screws): bend its tabs to about 80° and insert it in the 4" exhaust, tabs toward you. If flames still lift after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent, shut off the gas and call a qualified service technician.

Annual checks: main burner lights within (4) seconds of the main valve opening; flame failure response de-energizes the safety shutoff in no more than (30) seconds.

panels.title: Pilot won't light
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power or use battery back-up
Wiring disconnected → check connections against the wiring schematic; on battery back-up, make sure batteries are fully charged
Gas supply off → check every shut-off between the appliance and the main line

panels.title: Pilot won't stay lit
items: No propane in tank → check and refill
Low gas pressure (bent line, undersized pipe, low line pressure) → consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot flame not on the rectification sensor → adjust the pilot screw on the valve (clockwise decreases, counterclockwise increases)
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten

panels.title: Main burner won't light
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch to ON
Gas off or low supply → check for multiple shut-offs, the propane tank, consult the supplier
Faulty wiring, plugged main burner orifice, or pilot flame not directed to the burner
Remote not working → replace batteries; no call for heat → remote ON, thermostat operation OFF

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: No propane in tank, or glass assembly installed incorrectly
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust or clear debris
Wrong pitch on horizontal venting → ¼" rise per foot required
Inner vent pipe leaking exhaust into the firebox, or excessive draft → repair, adjust the restrictor

codes: Backup pack under 4V; low double-beep on ON/OFF — replace batteries
No ignition after two tries — check gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset or re-initialize

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights its own pilot with an electronic igniter. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday use

Press ON/OFF on the remote. A beep confirms the command. About 4 seconds later the igniter starts sparking to light the pilot, and the pilot lights the burner. The main ON/OFF rocker switch on the control must be set to ON.

After the gas has been off

  1. Press the remote's OFF button and turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  2. Turn the manual gas valve your technician installed clockwise to OFF. Use only your hand, never tools.
  3. Wait five minutes, then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  4. Turn the valve counterclockwise to ON, turn the power back on and press ON.
Won't light? The control sparks for about 60 seconds, pauses about 35 seconds, then tries once more. If that fails it locks out and the red light blinks 3 times. Turn it off with the remote, wait about 2 seconds and turn it on again. Still nothing? Turn off the gas to the fireplace and call your service technician or gas supplier.

Turning off the gas

Press OFF on the remote, turn off the power if service is planned, then turn the manual valve clockwise to OFF.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs the fireplace once the main ON/OFF rocker switch on the control is set to ON. A single beep confirms each command.

  • ON/OFF — turns the fireplace on (it starts its lighting sequence) and off.
  • Up / Down arrows — 6 flame levels. Down steps the flame lower until it's off; Up steps it higher. If the flame is off while the system is on, Up relights it on HI.
  • Thermostat key — press once to use the remote as a room thermostat set to the temperature you choose. Press until SMART appears to have the flame turned down automatically as the room reaches your set point; manual flame control is off in SMART. Set the temperature with the arrows.
  • Mode key — steps to the fan (6 speeds) and accent light (6 levels), if fitted. Adjust with the arrows.

Handy extras

  • Key lock to avoid unsupervised use: press Mode and Up together. A lock icon appears; repeat to unlock.
  • °F / °C: with the system off, press Thermostat and Mode together.
  • A battery icon means the remote's 3 AAA batteries are low.
Burner won't come on? Make sure the remote is on and thermostat operation is turned off — otherwise there may be no call for heat.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
Foggy glass

When the fireplace is first lit, condensation appears on the glass. This is normal in all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

A paint smell is normal during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during this time to help the paint cure faster.

Ticks and pings

The metal expands and contracts as it heats and cools, so you may hear noises. That's normal and doesn't affect performance or how long the fireplace lasts.

Blue flames at first

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow.

Beeps, pauses and the fan

  • One beep means the fireplace received a remote command. A low double-beep means the backup batteries are low.
  • When the pilot has been lit continuously, the system switches off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours to run a safety check, then goes back to its last command.
  • In thermostat mode the fan starts about 5 minutes after the fire lights and runs about 12 minutes after it's turned off.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is a homeowner job, about once a year. Do it only when the fireplace is completely cool — never remove or clean the glass while it's hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Remove the safety screen by lifting it up and out of its slots.
  3. Pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down, then lift the glass assembly up and off the 2 tabs at the top.
  4. Clean with a suitable fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. Refit it: set the slots at the top over the tabs, lower the bottom into place, then pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  6. Put the safety screen back before you use the fireplace.
Never run it with the glass off, cracked or broken. Don't strike or slam the glass, and wear protective gloves to handle broken glass. Replacement glass (#700-179T) comes only from Hussong Mfg. as a complete assembly and should be fitted by a qualified service person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
Your fireplace can run its pilot two ways. You choose with the remote.

IPIspark-to-pilot: the igniter lights the pilot each time the fireplace turns on
CPIcontinuous (standing) pilot that stays lit

Why choose CPI? A standing pilot keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the main burner lights with less air-flow disruption.

To switch

  1. With the fireplace off, press Mode until the CPI icon is selected.
  2. Press Up to turn CPI on, or Down to go back to IPI. A single beep confirms.

With the fireplace on, a snowflake icon on the remote's screen means CPI is active; no snowflake means IPI.

7-day timeout: in CPI, if the main burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off as a safety feature. Any burner ignition restarts the 7-day count.

If the pilot never goes out, the system is set to CPI. Switch to IPI.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house power and has a battery backup pack, so the burner still works in a power outage.

Backup pack (control module)4 × AA, not included
Remote3 × AAA, included

During an outage

  • Battery backup runs the burner only. The fan and accent light won't work until power returns.
  • How long backup batteries last depends on their quality, the number of ignitions and other factors.

Low-battery signs

  • Backup pack: a low double-beep when you press ON/OFF, and the red light blinks once at intervals. After that alert, no commands are accepted until you replace the batteries. A beep at power-up confirms the new ones.
  • Remote: a battery icon shows on the screen before the power runs out. It goes away once you replace them.

The backup holder is on the control module, and the manual reaches the control module housing by removing the bottom frame: take off the safety barrier, lift the bottom frame up and out of its slots, and put both back afterwards.

The fireplace's power supply is meant to stay live at all times and has no wall switch. Turn the power off only when the lighting or service steps tell you to.

flame.title: Flames, logs & soot
flame.html:
The look you want is lazy, yellow flames. That needs no adjustment.

  • When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow.
  • Flames should be steady, not lifting or floating.
  • If your vent ends with a vertical (upward) termination, the flame may look more active and compact.
  • You can choose from 6 flame levels on the remote.

When to call for service

Call a qualified service technician if the flames stay blue, turn dark orange with black tips, or lift off the burner, or if soot builds up on the glass. The manual traces soot to log placement, the burner's air setting (venturi), and vent cap or vent pitch problems. Venturi adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician.

About your logs: the fireplace uses an 8-piece set — traditional logs (#B41-500) or birch logs (#B41-B501). Logs must not sit over the burner ports; wrong placement causes excessive soot on the logs and glass.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building immediately.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell around the fireplace, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low.

Everyday safety

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety barrier on. If it's damaged, replace it with a Hussong Mfg. barrier made for this fireplace.
  • Supervise young children in the same room. A safety gate can keep toddlers and other at-risk people away.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, drapes, gasoline and other flammables away.
  • Never burn wood, paper or any other solid fuel in it.
  • Turn the gas valve by hand only — never with tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it; call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpet or bedding can mean cleaning more often.

Glass cleaningYou · annually
Firebox cleaning, glass latch checkService person · annually
Fan vacuumingService person · every 6 months
Vent system checkService person · annually
Burner and pilot checkService person · annually
Glass inspection for cracks or nicksService person · annually

Control compartments, burners and air passages must be kept clean; a vacuum is used on all components. The fan's bearings are sealed and need no oiling.

Any safety screen or barrier removed for service must go back on before the fireplace is used.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants your Kozy Heat fireplace to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase.

30 days · parts & laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborAll other parts and material, subject to exclusions
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. You don't need to send anything in to register. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model, and contact your authorized dealer within 30 days of noticing a defect.

What voids or limits it

  • Installation by anyone but a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not following the manual
  • Removing the serial number or testing label, or altering the fireplace
  • Submersion, long periods of dampness, or water damage
  • Installation and operating problems such as environmental conditions, inadequate venting or negative air pressure; chimney components and non-Hussong accessories aren't covered
This is a summary. The full terms are on the warranty page.

specManifold.html:

Valve taps: OUT (B) is manifold, IN (A) is inlet. Light the pilot, open the OUT tap counterclockwise, attach a manometer on a ¼" I.D. hose, light the burner and read. Lifting (ghosting) flames can mean gas pressure is too high — check the manometer readings.

Non-combustible mantel: min 6" vertical clearance to a max 6" depth, then 1" up per 1" deeper. Barrier gasket rope, if present, must touch the face to achieve these mantel clearances.

Table 3.1 (p. 13) prints 356mm with this 9" mantel clearance; section 4.1.1 (p. 18) gives 9" (229mm).

Floor protection in front isn't required. Barrier B41-PTF2 needs the unit 2-1/4" above the hearth and 3" from its outside edge to a sidewall.

A single vertical header board is required to maintain clearances. Allow for wall covering and facing thickness, and adjust for a hearth. Metal-Fab rear vent: add 3-3/4" to the enclosure depth. Masonry facing needs a foundation for the full load and a lintel over the unit.

Set on a level surface able to carry the unit and venting — not directly on carpet, vinyl or other combustibles other than wood; use a metal or wood panel the full width and depth. Above floor level, build a solid, continuous platform.

Maker's website: Electronic Ignition, IPI or Millivolt. This manual describes only the IPI (Proflame 2) control.

The supply must be hot at all times with no switch in it; shut off the breaker before working on it. Ground per local code, or ANSI/NFPA 70 or CSA C22.1. The three-prong grounding plug goes directly into a properly grounded receptacle — never cut the ground prong. Battery backup runs the burner only; the optional fan and light don't operate on it. Don't use the unit if any part has been under water: immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

conflicts.issue: Mantel clearance for a 6" deep mantel: Table 3.1 gives 9" (356mm); section 4.1.1 gives 9" (229mm).

review.notes: Manual covers BAY-41-L (traditional log set B41-500) and BAY-41-BW (birchwood log set B41-B501) with one SIT Proflame 2 IPI control (CPI selectable); no millivolt version is described, though the catalog lists 'IPI or millivolt'. Not in the manual, so not checked: efficiency (catalog 72.19 / 72.16% AFUE), weight (199 lb), view area, the Minnesota 50-pascal claim. Catalog height / width / depth (34.5 / 40.75 / 17 in) match values printed on Figure 2.1 (p. 9), but the figure's labels are not readable as text, so overall dimensions are not transcribed; the guide gives the Table 3.1 rough opening instead. Table 5.1 (p. 25) prints 'recommended' under the propane row with no clear value; the guide gives propane 12" - 13" WC min - max only (Table 11.1, p. 50). Figure-only content not transcribed: log placement (Fig. 8.3 / 8.4), typical installation and framing drawings, the shaded venting areas (Fig. 7.2 / 7.3), the termination-location diagram, wiring schematic. Manual typos: p. 11 'B41-PFT2' (parts list B41-PTF2); p. 30 cites 'Section 7.8 ... page 29' for the #700-2 kit (it is 7.9, p. 38); section 10.9.5 'Turn OFF' repeats the turn-ON wording; Fig. 2.1 pairs 28 3/8" with 955mm (not used).
